inbound_firewall_enabled.title: Inbound Firewall Enabled
inbound_firewall_enabled.description: Whether an inbound firewall or network access control policy is actively enforced on this resource or network boundary

default_inbound_policy.title: Default Inbound Policy
default_inbound_policy.description: The default action applied to inbound traffic that does not match any explicit rule — determines whether unauthorized connections are blocked by default

unrestricted_inbound_ports.title: Unrestricted Inbound Ports
unrestricted_inbound_ports.description: List of ports (or port ranges) that are open to all source IPs (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0) on inbound rules, indicating over-permissive exposure

egress_filtering_enabled.title: Egress Filtering Enabled
egress_filtering_enabled.description: Indicates whether outbound traffic filtering rules are actively enforced on the firewall or security group

default_egress_policy.title: Default Egress Policy
default_egress_policy.description: The default action applied to outbound traffic that does not match any explicit allow rule

permitted_egress_destinations.title: Permitted Egress Destinations
permitted_egress_destinations.description: List of explicitly allowed outbound destination CIDRs or address groups. An entry of '0.0.0.0/0' or '::/0' indicates unrestricted outbound access.

stateful_inspection_enabled.title: Stateful Inspection Enabled
stateful_inspection_enabled.description: Indicates whether the firewall performs stateful packet inspection, tracking connection state and validating packets against known session state tables. Also used for inter-segment traffic inspection.

permitted_connection_states.title: Permitted Connection States
permitted_connection_states.description: List of connection states explicitly allowed by firewall rules (e.g., ESTABLISHED, RELATED, NEW). Proper stateful configuration requires at minimum ESTABLISHED and RELATED states to be permitted while NEW is controlled.

stateless_packet_acceptance_enabled.title: Stateless Packet Acceptance Enabled
stateless_packet_acceptance_enabled.description: Indicates whether the firewall accepts inbound packets without validating connection state, which would allow stateless packet forgeries to bypass the firewall.

logging_enabled.title: Logging Enabled
logging_enabled.description: Whether logging is enabled on the firewall rule configuration to record allow and deny decisions

log_both_allow_and_deny.title: Log Both Allow and Deny Actions
log_both_allow_and_deny.description: Whether the logging configuration captures both permitted (allow/accept) and denied (drop/reject) traffic decisions, ensuring complete audit coverage

log_destination.title: Log Destination
log_destination.description: Where firewall log records are sent — determines whether logs are retained in a queryable, durable store or only held locally

default_deny_rule_present.title: Default Deny Rule Present
default_deny_rule_present.description: Indicates whether a default-deny (deny-all) rule exists as the final rule in the firewall policy, ensuring all unmatched traffic is blocked.

default_rule_action.title: Default Rule Action
default_rule_action.description: The action applied by the default (catch-all) firewall rule when no other rule matches traffic.

implicit_permit_rules_present.title: Implicit Permit Rules Present
implicit_permit_rules_present.description: Indicates whether any implicit (non-explicitly-defined) permit rules exist in the firewall policy that could allow unintended traffic through without explicit administrator approval.

wildcard_source_rules_present.title: Wildcard Source Address Rules Present
wildcard_source_rules_present.description: Indicates whether any permit rules use wildcard or any-source (0.0.0.0/0 or 'any') as the source address, creating overly permissive inbound access.

wildcard_destination_port_rules_present.title: Wildcard Destination Port Rules Present
wildcard_destination_port_rules_present.description: Indicates whether any permit rules allow traffic to any destination port (e.g., port range 0-65535 or 'any port') rather than scoping to specific required service ports.

protocol_any_permit_rules_present.title: Protocol-Any Permit Rules Present
protocol_any_permit_rules_present.description: Indicates whether any permit rules use protocol 'any' or 'all' rather than specifying the required protocol (TCP, UDP, ICMP, etc.), allowing unrestricted protocol access.

overly_broad_permit_rule_count.title: Count of Overly Broad Permit Rules
overly_broad_permit_rule_count.description: The number of permit rules that combine wildcard source, wildcard destination, or unscoped port/protocol definitions, indicating failure to apply least-privilege scoping.

segment_isolation_rules_configured.title: Segment Isolation Rules Configured
segment_isolation_rules_configured.description: Indicates whether explicit firewall rules exist to control traffic between network segments (e.g., DMZ, internal, trusted, untrusted zones)

default_inter_segment_policy.title: Default Inter-Segment Traffic Policy
default_inter_segment_policy.description: The default action applied to traffic crossing segment boundaries when no explicit rule matches

unrestricted_segment_pairs.title: Unrestricted Segment Pairs
unrestricted_segment_pairs.description: List of network segment pairs (e.g., 'DMZ->Internal', 'Guest->Corporate') that have no filtering rules applied between them

rule_versioning_enabled.title: Rule Versioning Enabled
rule_versioning_enabled.description: Whether the firewall platform stores versioned snapshots of rule configurations, enabling historical comparison and rollback.

change_approval_process.title: Change Approval Process
change_approval_process.description: The formality of the change approval workflow applied to firewall rule modifications.

rollback_capability.title: Rollback Capability Available
rollback_capability.description: Whether a tested and documented rollback procedure exists to revert firewall rules to a prior known-good state.

configuration_drift_detection.title: Configuration Drift Detection
configuration_drift_detection.description: Whether automated tooling detects and alerts on unauthorized or unplanned changes to firewall rules.

icmp_filtering_enabled.title: ICMP Filtering Enabled
icmp_filtering_enabled.description: Indicates whether the firewall actively filters and restricts ICMP traffic, blocking unnecessary ICMP types and subtypes that can be used for covert channels or tunneling.

protocol_anomaly_filtering_enabled.title: Protocol Anomaly Filtering Enabled
protocol_anomaly_filtering_enabled.description: Indicates whether the firewall blocks malformed or anomalous packets that exploit protocol header fields (e.g., IP options, unusual flag combinations, fragmentation abuse) for covert communication.

non_essential_protocols_blocked.title: Non-Essential Protocols Blocked
non_essential_protocols_blocked.description: Indicates whether uncommon or non-essential IP protocols (e.g., GRE without business justification, protocol 41 IPv6-in-IPv4 tunneling, etc.) that could be used for covert channels are explicitly denied.

siem_forwarding_enabled.title: SIEM Forwarding Enabled
siem_forwarding_enabled.description: Indicates whether the firewall is configured to forward deny events and anomaly detections to a centralized SIEM or logging platform in real time.

siem_destination_configured.title: SIEM Destination Configured
siem_destination_configured.description: Indicates whether a valid SIEM destination (IP/hostname and port) is configured for log/event forwarding.

forwarded_event_types.title: Forwarded Event Types
forwarded_event_types.description: List of event categories being forwarded to the SIEM, such as 'deny', 'anomaly', 'threat', 'policy_violation'.
